title: Rav Shmuel bar Yaakov
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Menachot 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.32a.3), and the Gemara brings proof from him for the words of Rava.

He is also mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 3:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.3.2.3), and [Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 3:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shevuot.3.8.3) (Hyman cites 3:9), where it is related that he saw a snake so large that it covered the royal wagon.
He is also mentioned in the Zohar, Chayei Sarah 124a, in the Midrash HaNe'elam.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The linked Menachot passage gives Rav Menashya bar Yaakov or, in an alternative attribution, Rav Shmuel bar Yaakov. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3372&lang=en) cites the same folio for Shmuel. Both linked Yerushalmi accounts report the sight of a snake’s hide. Hyman describes the snake covering the royal wagon.
Hyman prints קכד., rendered 124a. The Zohar edition is unspecified; the reference is to Midrash HaNe’elam within Chayei Sarah.
